cause-and-effect language
future forms and passive voice
gist and detail strategies
steps: Activate prior knowledge and inspect clues.
Identify the task purpose and evidence available.
Separate facts, interpretations and proposals.
Use target vocabulary/structures in context.
Check whether wording overstates certainty.
Revise or rehearse for clarity and audience.

workedExamples.title: Evidence before conclusion
workedExamples.example: A report says a town is testing a zero-waste collection system; it does not claim the system has solved all waste problems.
workedExamples.analysis: The supported conclusion is that a solution is being tested. Saying the problem is solved would go beyond the evidence.

workedExamples.title: Problem–solution link
workedExamples.example: A school wants to cut down on disposable cups. It proposes refill stations and tracks monthly cup use.
workedExamples.analysis: The proposal matches the identified consumption habit and includes a way to observe whether use changes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating one example as proof that a policy always works.
commonMistakes.correction: Use cautious language and state what the available evidence actually shows.

commonMistakes.mistake: Naming a solution without linking it to the stated problem.
commonMistakes.correction: Explain which cause, behaviour or impact the solution is intended to address.

Can I use at least two target terms accurately in context?
Have I avoided alarmist or absolute wording where the evidence is limited?

body: x, y, z harflerinin ses kullanımları ve sosyal ifadelerin doğal bağlamda kullanımı. Bu not, gelecek hakkında konuşurken kesin bilgi ile olasılığı ayırmayı esas alır. Teknoloji örnekleri yararların yanında mahremiyet, erişim, çevresel etki, güvenlik ve insan denetimi gibi sınırlılıklarla birlikte ele alınır. Öğrenci, kanıtın izin verdiği ölçüde may, might, could, likely, unlikely gibi ifadeleri seçer; henüz gerçekleşmemiş bir gelişmeyi kaçınılmaz gerçek olarak sunmaz.
objectiveText: Students can select and use target phonological aspects such as pronunciation and intonation of target sounds, words, phrases, clauses, and sentences in utterances authentically, naturally, and accurately in the current content about 'life in the universe and future with future lifestyles, future technologies and inventions' to develop holistic and conscious pronunciation skills after recognising them in context. | Students can construct meaningful spoken content about 'life in the universe and future with future lifestyles, future technologies and inventions' through efficient and meaningful practice. | Students can reconstruct the information about 'life in the universe and future with future lifestyles, future technologies and inventions' when communicating with others.

lessonSections.whatIWillLearn: Pronunciation and Social Language kapsamında tema dilini kanıta ve bağlama göre nasıl anlayıp üreteceğimi öğreneceğim.
lessonSections.priorKnowledge: Gelecek zaman ifadeleri, temel teknoloji sözcükleri, ana fikir-ayrıntı ayrımı ve bağlamdan anlam çıkarma bilgilerini hatırla.
steps: Bağlamı ve görevin amacını belirle.
Kanıt, olasılık ve varsayımı ayır.
Hedef sözcük veya yapıyı bağlam içinde seç.
Ürünü açıklık, doğruluk ve denge açısından kontrol et.

workedExamples.title: Evidence-aware claim
workedExamples.example: Solar panels could reduce a smart home’s grid use when sunlight and system capacity are sufficient.
workedExamples.analysis: Could olasılık bildirir; sonuç koşullara bağlanır ve kesin gelecek iddiası kurulmaz.

workedExamples.title: Balanced technology view
workedExamples.example: AI home assistants may save time, but users should also consider privacy settings and human control.
workedExamples.analysis: Yarar ve risk aynı bağlamda, ölçülü modal dil kullanılarak sunulur.

commonMistakes.mistake: Every future technology will definitely improve life.
commonMistakes.correction: Avoid inevitability; use evidence-based probability and name relevant conditions or trade-offs.

commonMistakes.mistake: A prediction is presented as a proven fact.
commonMistakes.correction: Separate what is observed now from what may or could happen later.
